_about: `roman` is the Telugu word (romanized) kept in the English sentence once the listener knows it; `start_known` words are kept from the start. Hard-coded words and phrases. `forms` are the spellings to match (put inflected forms like ఆటోలో too; a leading ^ means only at the start of what was said). `translate_as` replaces the match before translation so it always comes out the same (use plain English the grandkid understands; the card shows the Telugu name and picture); `translate_forms` overrides it per inflected form (ఆటోలో -> in an auto-rickshaw). `category` drives image cards (food, vehicle, place, clothing, festival) and explanation cards (family, idiom, slang). `note` is the one-line explanation shown on the card. `substitute: false` leaves a word for the translator (it already knows it) and `match_english` lists the English it may use.
